facts.value: Email marketing is a separate service. Current pricing says it is free up to 500 subscribers, with monthly or annual fees above that based on subscriber count.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: Conflict in public materials: ecommerce pricing says “no trial” and offers a free-to-start account; the Terms page includes a general 14-day free-trial clause that can convert to a paid subscription.

facts.label: Analytics plan access and add-on
facts.value: Dashboard charts and the storefront analytics integrations are not listed as paid add-ons; the public pricing page includes revenue insights and says there are no monthly ecommerce feature charges.

facts.label: Higher-volume merchants
facts.value: Lemon Squeezy invites large-volume, low-price or high-transaction businesses to contact sales for custom pricing.

facts.label: Email report plan boundary
facts.value: Email broadcast analytics are part of the separate email marketing module. Email plan level follows subscriber count; broadcast sending is limited to up to 10 times the plan's subscriber limit in a calendar month.

facts.label: Analytics usage limits and spend controls
facts.value: A hard cap, analytics overage, usage alert or spend-control setting for the dashboard was not found. Analytics is not priced by MRR, events, pageviews or users on the public pricing page.

facts.label: Email plan limit behavior
facts.value: Broadcast sends are limited to 10 times the subscriber allowance each calendar month. Importing subscribers above the current email plan's limit can automatically upgrade that plan.

facts.label: Stores per account
facts.value: A merchant can create and manage as many different stores as they like from one account.

facts.label: Seats and team access
facts.value: Team owners can invite store members. The public Teams docs allow multiple invitations but publish no seat cap or per-seat charge. Members cannot manage Teams, Billing, Plans or Payouts.

facts.label: Product allowances
facts.value: Lemon Squeezy says a store can have unlimited products and each product can have unlimited variants.

facts.label: Merchant eligibility and payout countries
facts.value: Merchants must be in a country where Lemon Squeezy can pay them through bank transfer or PayPal, and a new store needs product/compliance approval before live sales. The supported-country page lists bank payout countries and links to PayPal's 200+ country coverage.

facts.label: India payout restriction
facts.value: India appears in the bank payout list with a qualification: since May 2024, Stripe only accepts new Indian accounts by invitation, so merchants without pre-approval must use PayPal for payouts.

facts.label: Buyer-country exclusions
facts.value: Lemon Squeezy says it cannot accept buyer payments from the Central African Republic, Cuba, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Eritrea, Guinea-Bissau, Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, North Korea, Russia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria or Yemen.

facts.label: Product and business restrictions
facts.value: Live stores must pass identity and business checks. The company generally allows digital goods and software/SaaS, while prohibiting physical goods and a long list of regulated or unsupported products and services.

facts.label: Entry path
facts.value: Free self-serve account and test mode; no card is required to sign up. To process live sales, merchants must activate a store and pass review.

facts.label: Category and directory overlap
facts.value: Primary category: revenue and subscription analytics built into an ecommerce/merchant-of-record platform. It overlaps payment processing, digital-product sales and subscription billing. It also has an optional storefront/checkout analytics connection to Google Analytics and Meta Pixel.

facts.label: Other built-in reporting features
facts.value: Separate Lemon Squeezy modules also report email campaign recipients, opens, clicks, unsubscribes and delivery issues, and affiliate pages report clicks, referrals and payouts.

facts.label: Supported platforms
facts.value: Hosted seller dashboard and store management are web-based. Stores can use Lemon Squeezy hosted storefronts and hosted or overlay checkouts; checkout links can also be placed on a merchant's own website or app.

facts.label: Dashboard languages
facts.value: A complete list of seller-dashboard languages was not found in the product, help or developer docs checked. Checkout localization launched with 34 languages; that is checkout language support, not proof of dashboard localization.

facts.label: Deployment editions
facts.value: The service is a hosted web SaaS. No vendor-supported self-hosted or private-deployment edition was found in the current product docs.

facts.label: Built-in website reports
facts.value: The main dashboard shows business metrics such as recent revenue and customer numbers, not a documented native traffic-source, visitor, country, device or landing-page report.

facts.label: Storefront and checkout tracking integration
facts.value: Optional Google Analytics and Meta Pixel integrations send page views and ecommerce events for Lemon Squeezy storefronts and hosted/overlay checkouts. Google Analytics event payloads include transaction ID, order total, tax total and currency. Events include item views/selections, cart, discount, payment information and purchase; Meta gets PageView, ViewContent, InitiateCheckout, AddToCart, discount, payment information and Purchase events.

facts.label: Email-campaign reports
facts.value: Broadcast reports provide an over-time chart and campaign stats for recipients, opens, clicks, unsubscribes and issues such as bounces or spam reports.

facts.label: Product usage reports and identity
facts.value: App event capture, funnels, retention cohorts and anonymous-to-known app-user analysis are not part of the documented seller dashboard. Customer revenue and subscription records are billing data, not product-usage analytics.

facts.label: Replays and heatmaps
facts.value: Session replay, heatmaps and interaction recordings are not applicable to this billing-derived analytics product; no such feature appears in the analytics docs checked.

facts.label: Native mobile analytics SDK
facts.value: A native iOS or Android analytics SDK, mobile offline event queue or native replay feature is not applicable to the revenue dashboard.

facts.label: Dashboard measures
facts.value: The dashboard can show new subscriptions, subscription renewal revenue, MRR, ARR, subscription churn rate and trial conversion rate. The general home dashboard also shows recent revenue and customer numbers.

facts.label: MRR/ARR metric methodology
facts.value: Since May 2025, the new “Monthly Recurring Revenue” and “Annual Recurring Revenue” charts use daily snapshots, account for recurring percentage discounts, multiple quantities and billing intervals, and distinguish discounted and pre-discounted values. Existing merchants retain the former real-time-style charts under “Cumulative MRR” and “Cumulative ARR”; new merchants get the revised charts by default.

facts.label: Customer-level revenue
facts.value: Customer API exposes total_revenue_currency and mrr as positive integer cents in USD, plus formatted values.

facts.label: Order revenue, tax and refunds
facts.value: Order API exposes order-currency and USD subtotal, discount, tax, total and refunded amount; order statuses include paid, refunded and partial refund.

facts.label: Refund treatment in dashboard metrics
facts.value: Whether dashboard revenue charts subtract partial and full refunds, tax, or fees from their totals was not specified in the chart or API metric documentation reviewed.

facts.label: Currency fields in the API
facts.value: Customer MRR and total-revenue fields are defined in USD cents. Order records preserve values in both the order currency and USD.

facts.label: Store currency and transaction currency
facts.value: The selected store currency is used throughout the Lemon Squeezy dashboard and checkout, but all checkout transactions are processed in USD; payouts are made in USD or converted by the payout processor to the merchant's selected payout currency.

facts.label: Subscription status coverage
facts.value: Subscription records identify trial, active, paused, past-due, unpaid, cancelled and expired states, plus billing interval, dates and payment processor. Billing intervals can be daily, weekly, monthly or yearly.

facts.label: Churn and trial-conversion definitions
facts.value: The dashboard offers subscription churn and trial conversion charts, but the public chart docs do not state the denominator, period boundary or treatment of paused, trial and cancelled subscriptions for these two rates.

facts.label: Revenue and order insight claims
facts.value: Current pricing also promotes real-time revenue insights including MRR, refunds, average order value and other business metrics.

facts.label: Billing sources and boundaries
facts.value: Native revenue records are organized as Lemon Squeezy stores, customers, orders and subscriptions. Subscription objects identify Stripe or PayPal as the underlying payment processor. No ongoing external billing-provider connector for the Lemon Squeezy dashboard was documented.

facts.label: Core setup
facts.value: Create an account and store. The account starts in Test mode; live selling requires store activation and review. The seller home dashboard is part of the account, and its charts are configurable.

facts.label: Optional web analytics setup
facts.value: To send storefront/checkout data to Google Analytics or Meta, add the matching Measurement ID or Pixel ID in Design settings and enable its toggle.

facts.label: API and event integration
facts.value: Merchants can use authenticated APIs for customer/order/subscription records and webhooks to receive store events; API keys are created in account settings.

facts.label: Visitor tracking completeness
facts.value: Lemon Squeezy warns that browser ad blockers can prevent the Google Analytics/Meta Pixel events from being tracked for some visitors.

facts.label: Revenue metric completeness and sampling
facts.value: The public dashboard and metric pages do not specify sampling, duplicate handling, internal/test-data filters for every chart, or an accuracy/completeness guarantee. Test mode is described as separate from live data.

facts.label: Browser script or SDK weight
facts.value: Not applicable to built-in revenue charts, which are viewed in the hosted seller dashboard. Lemon Squeezy does not publish byte size for the optional Google/Meta integrations on the pages checked.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep and requirements
facts.value: Not applicable: the documented service is hosted by Lemon Squeezy or its agents; no supported self-host deployment or installation guide was found.

facts.label: Identifiers and browser storage
facts.value: Core merchant reports use store/customer/order records. The optional GA and Meta integrations use those third-party platforms' tracking; Lemon Squeezy's integration docs do not specify their cookie, device identifier or cross-device behavior.

facts.label: Consent and controls
facts.value: The integration guide documents enabling GA/Meta IDs but does not describe a consent manager, consent-mode behavior, regional defaults or a no-banner/legal exemption claim.

facts.label: Data location and agreements
facts.value: Terms describe a hosted service running on Lemon Squeezy or agent servers. The privacy page says data can be stored/processed in the United States or where the company and its partners/processors have facilities. The DPA says transfers outside the EEA require prior written consent and safeguards.

facts.label: Data processing agreement and processors
facts.value: A public DPA is available. Its processor clause says no subprocessor may be appointed or given Company Personal Data unless required or authorized by the company. The privacy policy lists Mailchimp as a third party currently used.

facts.label: Named subprocessor inventory
facts.value: A current complete list of subprocessors and their processing locations was not found in the public DPA, privacy policy or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Stripe affiliate location and role
facts.value: Stripe's current affiliate page lists Sold Through Link, LLC (fka Lemon Squeezy, LLC) in the United States for merchant-of-record-related services.

facts.label: Customer and order data
facts.value: Public customer API examples include name, email, city, region, country, store ID, total revenue and MRR. Order API includes order and customer IDs, amounts, currency, discount, tax, status and refund values.

facts.label: Website/device log data
facts.value: The privacy policy says Lemon Squeezy may collect website log data such as IP address, browser type/version, pages visited and visit time, plus device type, operating system and unique device identifiers.

facts.label: Deletion controls
facts.value: The DPA provides for deletion/return of Company Personal Data within 10 business days after cessation of the relevant service, subject to its terms. The privacy policy says account personal information is deleted within 30 days after account deletion, with legal/accounting exceptions.

facts.label: Analytics and order history retention
facts.value: No public retention duration was found for dashboard charts, historical MRR snapshots or order exports while an account is active. The privacy policy gives a general “as long as needed” rule and permits legal/accounting retention.

facts.label: Cancellation and post-termination access
facts.value: Terms say the customer has no access to Customer Data after termination and is responsible for copying or removing it before termination. The DPA and privacy policy describe separate deletion timelines after service/account cessation.

facts.label: Email report history
facts.value: The broadcast report page explains the metrics available but does not state how long campaign reports, opens or clicks remain available after sending or after an email plan is cancelled.

facts.label: Order CSV export
facts.value: A seller can export store orders to CSV from the Orders page; Lemon Squeezy emails the download. The documented columns include product/variant, customer and location fields, currency, subtotal, discount, tax, total and date.

facts.label: API access and limits
facts.value: The authenticated REST API exposes paginated store, customer, order and subscription resources. Public API docs state a limit of 300 calls per minute and maximum page size of 100.

facts.label: Analytics-specific export
facts.value: A dedicated CSV or API endpoint for dashboard chart aggregates/MRR snapshots was not identified. Underlying customer/order/subscription records are available through the API; the exact dashboard chart export path is not documented in the pages checked.

facts.label: Email subscriber export
facts.value: Email subscriber lists can be exported as CSV with subscriber status, email, country (when available), email sends, opens, clicks and dates.

facts.label: Stripe migration
facts.value: Lemon Squeezy offers a support-assisted Stripe migration for products, prices, customers, payment methods, invoices, subscriptions and coupons.

facts.label: Paddle migration
facts.value: Lemon Squeezy offers a support-assisted Paddle migration, including products, customers, payment methods, transactions, subscriptions, coupons and license keys; transactions map to Lemon Squeezy orders.

facts.label: Gumroad migration
facts.value: Gumroad migration is available as a manual CSV-assisted process for sales, products, customers and license keys. The guide says there is no direct subscription migration route from Gumroad.

facts.label: Imported history in analytics
facts.value: The public migration guides do not specify whether migrated invoices/transactions backfill the built-in revenue, MRR/ARR or churn charts, or how imported dates affect chart history.

facts.label: Identity and lifecycle
facts.value: Lemon Squeezy is an active hosted ecommerce and payments platform. Stripe announced its acquisition on July 26, 2024. Current Lemon Squeezy terms name Sold through Link, LLC (f/k/a Lemon Squeezy LLC), a Utah LLC; Stripe's affiliate list names Sold Through Link, LLC (fka Lemon Squeezy, LLC) as a US merchant-of-record affiliate.

facts.label: Current availability and shutdown check
facts.value: Public self-serve pricing and signup, product docs, API docs and Lemon Squeezy status page were live when checked. The status page listed app, API, docs and checkout components and no incident in its prior 7 days. The Lemon Squeezy blog/archive and Stripe newsroom were checked; no Lemon Squeezy shutdown or sunset notice was found.

facts.label: Stripe Managed Payments relationship
facts.value: Stripe Managed Payments is Stripe's merchant-of-record product built by the Lemon Squeezy team. Stripe's June 2026 newsroom says it is generally available to German businesses for sales into 195 markets. Lemon Squeezy's January post described public access as upcoming and an easy migration route as a goal.

facts.label: Source license
facts.value: Not applicable to the public offer: no self-hosted code edition or product source repository is offered in the pages checked.

facts.label: Public docs and support
facts.value: Public getting-started, help, developer and API docs, changelog and status page are available. Pricing says support is available through its help center, with a stated response time of 24–48 hours.

facts.label: Public interactive dashboard demo
facts.value: A public no-account interactive seller dashboard was not identified on the home, pricing, docs, blog or help pages checked.

facts.label: Billing meter and currency
facts.value: Standard Paddle Checkout pricing is 5% of the transaction’s suggested retail price plus USD $0.50 per checkout transaction. Paddle can offer custom pricing for high-volume or complex businesses.

facts.label: Paddle Invoicing fee
facts.value: Paddle’s seller agreement states a 3.5% fee on Paddle Invoicing transactions paid by bank transfer.

facts.label: Monthly or migration fees
facts.value: Public pricing says no monthly fees or migration fees and describes an all-inclusive transaction price.

facts.label: Separate analytics free plan
facts.value: No standalone free Paddle Billing Reporting plan was found. The built-in reports are part of a Paddle Billing account, whose public tariff has no monthly fee but does charge transaction fees when used for sales.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: A time-limited trial for Paddle Billing reporting was not published in the pricing, reporting or onboarding pages checked. Sandbox is documented for testing, not as a paid-service trial.

facts.label: Reports included with Billing
facts.value: Paddle describes dashboard reporting and downloadable reports as part of Paddle Billing. Pricing lists the all-in-one billing platform with no monthly fee and no separate report or Explore price.

facts.label: Custom merchant pricing
facts.value: Paddle offers custom pricing for high-volume businesses or complex business models; no fixed public quote was listed.

facts.label: Optional advisory service
facts.value: The reporting page advertises bespoke SaaS analysis through a premium Advisory service, but the public pages checked do not show its price or scope for an individual account.

facts.label: ProfitWell Metrics cost
facts.value: ProfitWell Metrics is a separate subscription analytics module, available inside Paddle Billing without additional setup; its product terms state that Metrics is free.

facts.label: Report creation limit
facts.value: Paddle allows up to 100 reports per account per 24 hours through the API and dashboard.

facts.label: Analytics overage or forced upgrade
facts.value: No overage price or forced reporting-tier upgrade is published for exceeding report or Explore usage. The 100-report daily limit is a request cap, not a priced allowance.

facts.label: Seller spend controls
facts.value: A report-generation cost cap or Paddle Billing analytics budget alert was not found in the pricing, API or report pages checked.

facts.label: Dashboard team access
facts.value: Paddle supports team members and role-based permissions. Admins and Finance roles can access Reports; Subscription KPIs role can access Subscription Metrics.

facts.label: Seat quota and price
facts.value: A maximum team-member count or per-seat price was not published in the team-permission and pricing pages checked.

facts.label: Seller eligibility and verification
facts.value: Before acting as Merchant of Record, Paddle reviews the seller’s domain, identity and, where applicable, business information. Business verification is not required for individuals or sole traders.

facts.label: Seller country availability
facts.value: Paddle says it supports software businesses worldwide except listed unsupported countries and regions; the help page names Afghanistan, Belarus, Cuba, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Russia, Syria, Venezuela and other exclusions.

facts.label: Buyer market reach and restrictions
facts.value: Paddle says Billing can sell in over 200 countries and territories but blocks unsupported or sanctioned locations; the developer list is available through the countries endpoint.

facts.label: Product restrictions
facts.value: Paddle’s signup route says it exclusively supports SaaS and digital products, while placing products such as financial services, gambling, physical products, hosting and marketplaces under categories requiring restrictions or review.

facts.label: Entry path
facts.value: A seller can create a Paddle account through the self-serve route and use a sandbox; live payment processing requires account verification.

facts.label: Dashboard-only analytics access
facts.value: The reports are presented as features of a Paddle Billing seller account; no independent public account route for purchasing only the Reporting/Explore module was found.

facts.label: Primary category
facts.value: Billing-provider revenue reporting and financial reconciliation.

facts.label: Distinct reporting layers
facts.value: Paddle Billing provides account record exports and reconciliation reports, an Explore dashboard/API for flexible metrics, and integrated ProfitWell Metrics for subscription health and benchmarking.

facts.label: Supported seller products
facts.value: Paddle Billing is offered for SaaS, software and digital products, including mobile apps selling through Paddle; it is the seller’s billing and checkout platform rather than a general app-usage analytics SDK.

facts.label: Dashboard and technical access
facts.value: Reports are viewed in Paddle’s hosted seller dashboard and can also be generated or queried through the Paddle API.

facts.label: Dashboard language
facts.value: A complete language list for the seller dashboard and reporting interface was not found in the product, help or developer pages checked.

facts.label: Deployment edition
facts.value: Paddle Billing reporting is a vendor-hosted dashboard and API service. No self-hosted or private-deployment edition was found in the current billing, reporting or pricing pages checked.

facts.label: Native website traffic reports
facts.value: Paddle Billing is not documented as a general web-traffic analytics tool for pageviews, referrers, UTM campaigns or site visitors. Its checkout reports describe Paddle checkout sessions and conversion performance.

facts.label: Checkout conversion report
facts.value: Checkout reports provide one row per checkout session with conversion data and context such as theme, display mode and customer country.

facts.label: Product usage events and identity
facts.value: Not applicable as a product-usage analytics product: Paddle Billing reporting does not document app event funnels, user paths, behavioral cohorts or anonymous-to-login identity stitching.

facts.label: Replays and heatmaps
facts.value: Not applicable: no session replay, click map or scroll map feature is described in Paddle Billing reporting docs.

facts.label: Native mobile analytics SDK
facts.value: Not applicable to the reporting product. Paddle can process sales for mobile apps, but its reporting pages do not describe an SDK for collecting app-use events or native-app replay.

facts.label: Built-in CSV report set
facts.value: The Billing reports menu covers Transactions, Transaction line items, Adjustments, Adjustment line items, Products and prices, Discounts, Checkouts, Subscriptions, and Payout reconciliation.

facts.label: Transactions and line items
facts.value: Transaction reports include transaction status, customer and subscription identifiers, payment details and balance-currency subtotal, discounts, tax, total, Paddle fee and earnings. Line-item reports break transaction amounts down by product/price item.

facts.label: Adjustments and payout reconciliation
facts.value: Adjustment reports cover refunds, credits and chargebacks. Payout reconciliation reports itemize balance movements and fees to reconcile payout amounts with remittance reports.

facts.label: Subscription detail report
facts.value: Each subscription row describes current status, dates, billing cycle, items, trials, discounts, lifetime spend, refunds and chargebacks; financial values may include original transaction and balance-currency amounts.

facts.label: Explore metric set
facts.value: Explore charts Revenue, Transactions, Refunds, Chargebacks, Checkout conversion, MRR and MRR growth, with filters for date, billing frequency, product and country and a single breakdown dimension.

facts.label: Explore revenue definition
facts.value: Explore Revenue is transaction value less discounts, before tax, Paddle fees, refunds or chargebacks are deducted.

facts.label: Billing chart revenue definition
facts.value: The Billing metrics help article says its Revenue chart is product base cost less discounts, excludes tax and Paddle fees, and excludes refunds/chargebacks and free, trialing or unpaid subscriptions.

facts.label: MRR and MRR growth
facts.value: Explore defines MRR as total monthly recurring revenue from active subscriptions. MRR growth is new, expansion and reactivation revenue less contraction and churn.

facts.label: Currency scope
facts.value: Explore API currency values are returned in the seller’s balance currency. Transaction and subscription report schemas expose transaction and balance-currency values; conversions and field-specific null cases are documented.

facts.label: External billing coverage
facts.value: Core Paddle Billing reports and Explore query the account’s Paddle Billing data; no ongoing external processor connection is documented for these modules.

facts.label: ProfitWell Metrics difference
facts.value: ProfitWell Metrics offers MRR, churn, LTV, ARPU, cohort and segment reports, benchmarks, and integrations such as Slack, HubSpot, Intercom and Salesforce; it refreshes every 3–6 hours. Billing Reports instead export Paddle transaction entities and reconcile payouts; Explore provides account-scoped metric charts with a 24-hour refresh.

facts.label: Data source and setup
facts.value: Reporting is populated by Paddle Billing’s own checkout, invoicing, transaction and subscription records. Sellers can also consume Billing API/webhook data; a separate visitor-tracking script is not required to generate account reports.

facts.label: API and checkout setup
facts.value: Paddle.js is used for hosted checkout integration, while Reports and Explore have separate account API routes for exports and metrics.

facts.label: Report freshness
facts.value: Paddle says report data may be delayed up to 24 hours and excludes some entities created within the last 24 hours. Reports sort by last update, so date filters use entity update time.

facts.label: “Real-time” freshness claim
facts.value: The reporting product page calls the reporting real-time, while the report guide allows up to 24 hours of delay and Explore refreshes every 24 hours. The product page does not define a metric-specific real-time service level.

facts.label: Explore refresh and aggregation
facts.value: Explore refreshes on a 24-hour cycle and uses UTC. A record associated with multiple products can appear in multiple breakdown rows, so row totals can exceed the unbroken total; “Other” groups additional values.

facts.label: Sampling and bot filters
facts.value: No sampling, bot-filtering or test-transaction exclusion scheme for each report and Explore metric was established in the report and metric docs checked.

facts.label: Browser script weight
facts.value: Not applicable to account-side reports and metrics. No browser analytics script size is needed to use the reporting dashboard.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to the hosted service; no server or database requirements for a self-hosted Reporting edition were found.

facts.label: Browser identifiers and cookies
facts.value: Not applicable as a visitor analytics tracker: the reporting product is based on billing and checkout entities, not a public-page visitor ID or cross-site audience cookie.

facts.label: Consent and legal basis
facts.value: Paddle’s privacy pages describe its own processing and cookie controls; reporting documentation does not establish a universal consent exemption for a seller’s checkout or customer-data use.

facts.label: Data processing agreement
facts.value: Paddle publishes a DPA that treats Paddle.com Inc. as processor for Customer Personal Data and addresses subprocessors, transfers and deletion.

facts.label: Storage and processing locations
facts.value: The current privacy notice says data may be transferred among Paddle entities and third-party processors located anywhere in the world, with transfer safeguards. The DPA says database servers are in third-party data centers but does not name a hosting region.

facts.label: Data in reports
facts.value: Reports can contain customer identifiers/contact details, country, transaction and subscription status, product/price data, invoice details, payment values, taxes, fees, refunds and chargebacks.

facts.label: Buyer privacy request and retention
facts.value: Paddle provides a buyer data-deletion request route, but says it retains certain transactional data for five years to meet legal obligations.

facts.label: CSV availability window
facts.value: Generated CSV reports are available for download for 14 days; the signed report download URL expires after 3 minutes, and another URL can be requested until the report expiry.

facts.label: Explore lookback
facts.value: Explore dashboard queries cover up to two years of history; API and MCP queries reach up to 1,096 days (about three years).

facts.label: Subscription report history
facts.value: Subscription reports show each subscription’s current state, update daily, and cannot be generated for a past date.

facts.label: Account cancellation and data deletion
facts.value: The seller DPA permits return/deletion requests after service cessation subject to its stated process and legal-retention exception; the current seller terms and DPA do not give one universal retention duration for every report and account-data type.

facts.label: CSV and dashboard export
facts.value: Paddle generates UTF-8 comma-delimited CSV reports. The dashboard provides filters by report type, and the API can build, check and download reports.

facts.label: Reports API workflow
facts.value: The Reports API creates a pending report, provides status through report retrieval or a report.updated webhook, and returns a temporary download URL.

facts.label: Metrics API
facts.value: Fixed metrics endpoints return timeseries; Explore uses GET /metrics/explore/entities and POST /metrics/explore for filtered or broken-down data.

facts.label: API query limits
facts.value: Report generation is capped at 100 per 24 hours. Explore pages allow up to 50 segments and 10,000 datapoints per page; older than the supported lookback returns an error.

facts.label: Paddle Classic migration
facts.value: Paddle Billing can import selected subscriptions from Paddle Classic, but migration docs say historic reporting data is not ported and remains accessible in Paddle Classic.

facts.label: Third-party historical billing import
facts.value: The reviewed Billing report and Explore docs do not document an ongoing connector or generic historical import from Stripe or other processors into these reporting modules.

facts.label: Name and official URL
facts.value: Paddle Billing reporting; https://www.paddle.com/billing/reporting

facts.label: Monthly recurring revenue
facts.value: MRR is ongoing subscription net amount normalized to a month; yearly prices are divided by 12. Trialing subscriptions are excluded; paused and past-due subscriptions count until they end.

facts.label: Committed and trial MRR
facts.value: The dashboard separates Committed MRR, Trial MRR including canceled trials, and Trial Committed MRR; committed views exclude subscriptions or trials canceled within their committed period as documented.

facts.label: Subscription counts
facts.value: Active subscriptions count through period end until the subscription actually ends; new subscriptions count at first paid order; renewed subscriptions count renewal orders.

facts.label: ARPU and LTV
facts.value: ARPU is MRR divided by distinct paying subscribers in the interval, excluding trials. LTV is calculated as (ARPU minus cost per user) divided by churn rate; LTV returns zero when churn is zero.

facts.label: Cost Insights customer LTV
facts.value: Cost Insights describes customer lifetime value as cumulative profit since the customer signed up.

facts.label: LTV wording across dashboards
facts.value: The Analytics docs give an ARPU/churn formula; Cost Insights describes customer LTV as cumulative profit since signup.

facts.label: Churn and cancellation
facts.value: Canceled subscriptions are cancellations requested during the interval; churned subscriptions are paid periods that actually ended. Churn rate divides churned subscriptions by the active base at the interval start.

facts.label: Cancellation reasons
facts.value: Cancellation reasons include too expensive, missing features, switched service, unused, customer service, low quality, too complex and other/free-form or no reason.

facts.label: Gross revenue
facts.value: Revenue is the order subtotal before Polar fees and tax; counts completed orders including one-time, new subscription and renewal orders.

facts.label: Net revenue
facts.value: Net Revenue deducts Polar's platform fee and payment processor fee and is described as the amount paid out to the merchant.

facts.label: One-time orders and revenue
facts.value: The dashboard counts completed non-recurring product orders and reports their gross subtotal revenue separately from subscription orders.

facts.label: Checkout conversion
facts.value: Conversion is succeeded checkouts divided by all created checkouts; expired and abandoned checkouts remain in the denominator.

facts.label: Cost, margin and customer profit
facts.value: Cost Insights reports ingested costs, cost per customer, profit per customer, gross margin and customer lifetime value using events annotated with _cost.

facts.label: Refund effect on reports
facts.value: The pages checked describe refunds and refunded order statuses, but do not explain whether or how historical revenue, MRR or churn metrics are recomputed after a full or partial refund.

facts.label: Tax and currency treatment
facts.value: Orders retain the currency charged and tax amounts; Finance says multi-currency orders are converted to USD for settlement. The Metrics API says monetary values are returned in cents but does not identify the reporting currency used for aggregate metrics.

facts.label: Order definitions
facts.value: Orders represent paid transactions; examples include one-time purchases, new subscriptions, renewals, prorated subscription changes and usage charges.

facts.label: Merchant setup
facts.value: Metrics appear for the Polar organization's own checkout orders and subscriptions; customers are automatically recorded after purchases.

facts.value: Terms define GMV/revenue for fees as ecommerce revenue excluding taxes, collected and/or invoiced over the preceding 12 full calendar months across connected/reported activities and channels

facts.label: Impacted GMV distinction
facts.value: Calculator says the fee basis is impacted GMV and online-only teams are charged against online GMV even if the company has retail activity

facts.label: MCP / Data Platform price
facts.value: Calculator shows USD $500/month and 0.24% GMV capture for the displayed <$5M GMV selection

facts.label: BI / Insights price
facts.value: Calculator shows USD $625/month and 0.30% GMV capture for the displayed <$5M GMV selection

facts.label: Core / Insights & Actions price
facts.value: Calculator shows USD $750/month and 0.36% GMV capture for the displayed <$5M GMV selection

facts.label: Ultimate tier threshold
facts.value: Ultimate / Growth Insights ++ is shown as available for businesses with $10M+ GMV; no exact rate was displayed in accessible text

facts.label: Price naming conflict
facts.value: Main pricing page names Core Plan and Custom Plan; calculator lists MCP / Data Platform, BI / Insights, Core / Insights & Actions, Ultimate / Growth Insights ++, and Causal Lift

facts.value: Older official blog posts state 0.10–0.25% or 0.10–0.20% of impacted GMV, while the current calculator shows 0.24%, 0.30%, and 0.36% for three displayed tiers

facts.label: Currency and billing
facts.value: Calculator displays USD; Terms say vendor fees are denominated in USD, monthly invoices in advance, with conversion to another currency only where the plan allows

facts.label: Term and annual payment
facts.value: Calculator says rolling monthly or annual, with 60–90 day commitment and opt-out; annual prepayment offers 12 months for 10 months’ payment

facts.label: Contract and price updates
facts.value: Terms say monthly advance invoicing; plan upgrade is pro-rated, but downgrade cannot occur during a contractual period; pricing changes require 30 days’ notice

facts.label: Tax and late fees
facts.value: Fees exclude tax; late payment can suspend access and incur stated recovery interest/fees depending on provider entity

facts.label: Permanent free plan
facts.value: No permanent free tier or free-forever allowance was established in current pricing, calculator, or Terms checked

facts.label: Trial availability
facts.value: Official help docs refer to a Free Trial; Pixel and custom connectors are unavailable during that trial

facts.label: Trial duration and payment method
facts.value: Trial length, payment-card requirement, and what happens automatically at expiry were not found in public pages checked

facts.label: Trial history
facts.value: Historical data sync and full backfill require a paid plan; Pixel attribution also needs about two weeks to become reliable and is disabled during trial

facts.label: Current public bundle page
facts.value: Main pricing page presents Core Plan and Custom Plan; Core bundles Business Intelligence, AI Agents, and Data Activations, and says it saves 20% against individual product costs

facts.value: Custom connectors are for paid Polar plans and unavailable in the free trial; some connectors can cost extra based on connector complexity and company size

facts.label: Snowflake reader access
facts.value: Direct customer access to the managed Snowflake Reader Account is a paid add-on, not included in base subscription; it includes 70 credits/month

facts.label: Plan allowance language
facts.value: Main pricing page advertises unlimited users and unlimited historical data; calculator separately sets AI token and Snowflake credit caps

facts.label: GMV-band reassessment
facts.value: Provider reassesses GMV at each contractual period; an increase can adjust fees for following periods; reductions only apply after the current period

facts.label: Overage rule
facts.value: Some plans have usage caps; Terms reserve the right to invoice excess use at platform rates at the end of each calendar month

facts.label: AI token cap and overage
facts.value: Calculator shows 540M annual tokens for Core at the displayed <$5M GMV selection and $3.33 per 1M token overage/month

facts.label: Snowflake credit cap and overage
facts.value: Calculator shows Snowflake credits capped monthly; $250/month add-on for 70 credits and $4 per credit overage at displayed lower GMV selection

facts.label: Hard spend controls
facts.value: Public pages checked do not establish a customer-set hard cap or automatic stop for GMV, AI token, or Snowflake-credit overages

facts.label: User allowance
facts.value: Pricing page says unlimited users; Managing Users says any number of users can be invited at no extra cost

facts.label: User roles
facts.value: Default roles include Admin, Analyst, Viewer, and Connector; custom roles can restrict data exploration and AI access

facts.label: Multiple stores and sources
facts.value: Shopify accounts can be added more than once; views can segment store, region or business

facts.label: Project or store cap
facts.value: Public pages advertise unlimited users and history but do not give a numeric cap or universal included store/connector allowance

facts.label: Customer type
facts.value: Terms restrict use to business-to-business and professional purposes; a person may qualify when acting for a commercial or professional activity

facts.label: Contracting region
facts.value: Contracting entity is assigned by billing address: Polar Analytics Inc. or The Growth Team SAS

facts.label: Country and sanctions limits
facts.value: No exhaustive country, sanctions, or restricted-territory list found in Terms, demo, or public help pages checked

facts.label: Required store access
facts.value: Connecting Shopify requires an account and admin or staff permission to install and authorize the app

facts.label: Evaluation path
facts.value: Vendor offers a demo form and discussion of pricing, onboarding, business goals, and current data stack

facts.label: Signup and purchase
facts.value: Help content describes signing up for a Polar account; Terms describe online subscription confirmation and monthly billing

facts.label: Interactive product demo
facts.value: No login-free interactive production dashboard or sandbox demo was found; public evaluation is via a booked demo

facts.label: Primary job
facts.value: Unify ecommerce, sales, marketing, finance and customer data into analytics, reporting and AI-assisted business insights

facts.label: Revenue and attribution overlap
facts.value: Store and ad performance, revenue, customer value, acquisition, cross-channel attribution, margin, inventory and retention reporting

facts.label: Category distinction
facts.value: Ecommerce business intelligence and marketing attribution, not a standalone subscription billing provider or Polar.sh payment product

facts.label: Analytics boundary
facts.value: Combines store data and connected analytics sources; it is not a general-purpose product analytics event platform

facts.label: Primary store platform
facts.value: Shopify connector and Shopify app; Shopify store data is the base for core dashboards

facts.label: Other commerce platforms
facts.value: Connectors include Recharge, Amazon Seller Central and Amazon Vendor Central; broader marketplace and retail sources appear in the connector directory

facts.label: Website analytics source
facts.value: Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, Fairing, and Polar Pixel are listed under analytics and attribution

facts.label: Dashboard languages
facts.value: Account settings offer an interface language choice, but the complete supported-language list was not established in public pages reviewed

facts.label: Hosted edition
facts.value: Polar Analytics is a vendor-hosted platform with customer data hosted on Polar or its subcontractor infrastructure

facts.label: Self-hosted edition
facts.value: No customer-operated installation or self-hosted server edition found

facts.label: Core ecommerce reports
facts.value: Ready-made dashboards cover acquisition, retention, products, subscriptions, engagement, and custom reports

facts.label: Traffic and engagement reports
facts.value: GA4 connector provides sessions, engaged sessions, users, pageviews, engagement duration, bounce rate and pageviews/session

facts.label: Polar Pixel funnel
facts.value: Funnel tracks sessions, product page views, add-to-cart, checkout start and checkout completion

facts.label: Channel and campaign reports
facts.value: Acquisition reports include channel/campaign spend, conversions, ROAS, CAC, marketing journeys and order touchpoints

facts.label: Country and device dimensions
facts.value: GA4 connector supports country and device dimensions; Pixel/Shopify reports can filter by channel, campaign and landing-page path

facts.label: Custom dashboards and scheduled reports
facts.value: Custom tables, charts and metric cards can be built; dashboards can be scheduled to email or Slack

facts.label: Storefront pixel scope
facts.value: Polar Pixel collects ecommerce journeys and attribution, not a universal website traffic dashboard by itself

facts.label: Website limitations
facts.value: Shopify app pixel does not install on Amazon Seller, Facebook/Instagram Checkout, TikTok Shop, or Shopify Shop App; orders may still appear if synced through Shopify

facts.label: Customer reports
facts.value: Customer reports include new/returning buyers, repeat rate, cohort and lifetime value metrics

facts.label: Product reports
facts.value: Product/variant, SKU, collection and tag performance are available from Shopify product and order data

facts.label: Custom metric layer
facts.value: Users can define custom metrics, dimensions, and data settings for business-specific calculations

facts.label: Identity method
facts.value: Pixel assigns a Lifetime ID and can stitch sessions to a customer across devices when identity information is available

facts.label: General product event analytics
facts.value: No general-purpose app event SDK or automatic arbitrary product-event capture system was found; headless Pixel sends defined ecommerce page/cart/checkout events

facts.label: Session replay and heatmaps
facts.value: No session replay or heatmap product was found in current feature, help, or pricing pages reviewed

facts.label: Native mobile analytics SDK
facts.value: No native iOS/Android app analytics SDK found; standard Pixel is a Shopify web pixel and headless JavaScript SDK

facts.label: Revenue, sales and profit metrics
facts.value: Metrics include sales/revenue, gross profit, net profit, AOV, order count, discounts, refunds, COGS and margin

facts.label: Net revenue and refund dates
facts.value: Polar typically reports net revenue after discounts, refunds and cancellations; refunds are recorded on their transaction date

facts.label: Attribution models
facts.value: Pixel supports first click by default and configurable models including last click, linear and position-based models

facts.label: Attribution settings
facts.value: Users can set paid-only eligibility, lookback window, and cash versus accrual attribution date

facts.label: MRR and subscription data
facts.value: Recharge is a supported sales channel and Polar lists subscription reporting; a standalone general subscription MRR definition was not fully established in public metric pages checked

facts.label: Currency handling
facts.value: Account currency is configurable; Shopify values may be converted using consistent exchange rates and can differ from presentment currency

facts.label: Revenue source breadth
facts.value: Shopify, Amazon Seller/Vendor, Recharge, ads, email and GA4 can be connected; custom connector coverage may be separately charged

facts.label: Taxes in GMV and dashboard metrics
facts.value: Contract GMV excludes taxes; dashboard revenue definitions depend on source and configurable Data Settings

facts.label: Third-party data integrations
facts.value: OAuth/API connections aggregate sales, marketing, analytics, email, finance, fulfillment and support sources

facts.label: Custom integration
facts.value: Custom connectors are available on paid plans; team setup requires credentials or account access depending on source

facts.label: Pixel capture
facts.value: Shopify storefront uses Shopify App Pixel; headless stores use a JavaScript Pixel SDK and send defined Shopify-style events

facts.label: Campaign tagging
facts.value: Pixel attribution needs tracking parameters such as source and campaign; Google Ads tags can be configured automatically while many other sources require manual UTMs

facts.label: Manual data source
facts.value: Google Sheets connector can import offline spend and other custom data; custom connectors cover other APIs

facts.label: Pixel session definition
facts.value: Default session ends after 30 minutes inactive; vendor support can adjust the timeout up to 24 hours

facts.label: Pixel attribution completeness
facts.value: Pixel attribution rate is based on orders expected to be trackable through Shopify Web or Recharge; POS and unsupported checkout sales are excluded

facts.label: Undefined attribution percentages
facts.value: One official guide describes 10–15% undefined conversions as normal; another describes 15–20% as normal

facts.label: Bot traffic
facts.value: Polar Pixel exposes an Is Bot Session dimension to flag likely bot sessions but does not automatically filter those sessions

facts.label: GA4 differences and latency
facts.value: GA4 can miss consent-rejected/ad-blocked events, take up to 12 hours to process, and produce totals that vary by API breakdown; Polar says it does not recalculate GA4 values

facts.label: Data integrity coverage
facts.value: Automated integrity tests compare selected high-signal metrics with source APIs; coverage is curated and does not include all dashboard metrics

facts.label: Cross-tool metric differences

facts.label: Script or SDK weight

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Not applicable: no customer-run Polar Analytics server edition was found; provider hosts and maintains the platform

facts.value: Pixel creates a unique Lifetime ID to link returning visits and, when signals permit, customer journeys across sessions/devices

facts.value: Pixel guide says the Pixel may fire without waiting for consent when a country is not selected in Shopify Admin customer privacy settings

facts.value: Help center says cookie consent banners can block the Pixel; consent rejection and ad blockers can leave conversions unattributed

facts.label: Region selection and backups

facts.label: Data categories

facts.label: Storefront data

facts.label: Vendor site data
facts.value: Vendor Privacy Policy says its own site may collect browser, IP, timezone, cookies, pages/products viewed, referral/search terms, interactions and purchase/contact details

facts.label: Remove source data
facts.value: Deleting a connector removes its historical data from dashboards; pausing leaves history and stops new syncs

facts.label: Account and data subject requests
facts.value: Privacy Policy says users can request access, transfer or deletion by emailing DPO; it says response within 30 days

facts.label: Historical data allowance
facts.value: Pricing page states unlimited historical data; sync article says full-history import requires a paid plan

facts.label: Trial history
facts.value: Free Trial cannot use Polar Pixel, and full historical data import requires paid plan

facts.label: Contract end export window
facts.value: After termination customer must request data return within 30 days; provider then makes data available in structured machine-readable format

facts.label: DPA deletion
facts.value: On termination, Polar ceases processing and, on customer written request, returns or securely deletes/unreadably renders data, unless law permits/requires retention

facts.label: Backups and retention duration
facts.value: No separate backup retention or exact deletion completion period found beyond the return/deletion language and applicable-law exception

facts.label: CSV exports
facts.value: Custom table/chart data can be exported as CSV; up to 100,000 rows per download; in-app report display is up to 1,000 rows

facts.label: Scheduled and automated exports
facts.value: Automations can send dashboards/reports by email or Slack; MCP and n8n can automate analytics workflows

facts.value: Polar MCP/API can programmatically request reports and analytics using an authenticated token; base endpoint is https://api.polaranalytics.com/mcp

facts.label: API limits
facts.value: No request rate limit or plan-specific MCP quota was established in the API/help pages checked

facts.label: Snowflake raw access
facts.value: Paid Snowflake Reader Account offers a read-only view of raw and transformed customer data, 70 credits/month; extra credits are chargeable

facts.label: Contract data portability

facts.label: Export plan gate
facts.value: Reader Account access is paid add-on; public docs do not show whether every CSV/MCP feature is identical across all plan tiers

facts.label: Shopify history import
facts.value: Connector backfills store history as far as Shopify permits; first sync can take up to 24 hours depending on data volume

facts.label: Other connector history
facts.value: Connecting sources imports available historical data; full-history import requires a paid plan; source API limits can slow initial load

facts.label: Historical Universal Analytics
facts.value: Existing Universal Analytics data can be kept alongside GA4 by setting non-overlapping connector date ranges

facts.label: CSV or competitor migration
facts.value: No dedicated migration importer for another analytics vendor’s raw history was found; Google Sheets/custom connectors are documented for other data

facts.label: New-customer route
facts.value: Demo page invites business customers to discuss pricing, onboarding, and next steps; docs describe signup and online paid subscription

facts.value: No notice found in official blog, website, Terms, current press/funding article, or policy pages searched

facts.label: Fundraising notice
facts.value: Official blog announced an $18 million Series A on November 12, 2024

facts.label: Retired Starter and Scale plan names
facts.value: Stripe says the former Billing Starter and Scale tiers were replaced by a single Billing plan; current public pricing uses 0.7% pay-as-you-go plus optional annual monthly tiers

facts.label: Pay-as-you-go overage
facts.value: 0.7% continues to apply to monthly Billing volume; there is no listed monthly fee cap

facts.label: Pay-monthly overage
facts.value: 0.67% applies to Billing volume above the selected plan’s monthly volume tier

facts.label: Basic usage event allowance
facts.value: Basic Meters API billing is included in Billing pricing up to 100 million events per month; detailed usage billing through Metronome is separate

facts.label: Spend caps and alerts
facts.value: Hard caps, account-level Billing fee alerts, or spend-stop behavior for the published tiers were not established in the pricing and help pages checked

facts.label: Accounts and organization views
facts.value: Stripe Organizations can centralize multiple Stripe accounts; Stripe’s changelog says subscriptions and invoices can be centrally viewed across organization accounts

facts.label: Account, project, and seat limits
facts.value: Numeric account, project, or Dashboard-user allowances for Billing analytics were not published in the pricing and account pages checked

facts.label: Account country availability
facts.value: Stripe publishes a current country/region availability list. It includes standard supported markets, preview markets, and some “Extended network” entries; Stripe warns that availability varies by product. Billing-specific country eligibility is not exhaustively stated on the list.

facts.label: Account eligibility
facts.value: Stripe Services Agreement says the user must be a business, sole proprietor, governmental/public-sector entity, or nonprofit located where Stripe provides or approves the service; use is subject to approval

facts.label: Sanctions and prohibited locations
facts.value: Stripe prohibits dealings involving Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and Crimea, Donetsk, and Luhansk; it also restricts sanctioned persons and certain Russia/Belarus-related activity

facts.label: Foreign-country account prerequisites
facts.value: Opening an account in a country different from the primary business country requires a local legal entity, tax ID, physical address, phone, identity document, working website, and physical bank account, subject to listed exceptions

facts.label: Entry path
facts.value: Self-serve Stripe account start is offered; large-volume or unique Billing packages can contact Sales

facts.label: Primary job
facts.value: Manage recurring subscriptions, invoices, payment collection, and subscription revenue reporting

facts.label: Analytics scope and overlap
facts.value: Subscription performance, usage, revenue recovery, and billing benchmarks; overlaps with subscription revenue analytics and billing/payment services

facts.label: Product boundary
facts.value: Billing analytics describes subscription and billing activity; custom analysis across all Stripe data is offered through separately priced Stripe Sigma or Data Pipeline

facts.label: Supported operating platforms
facts.value: Stripe Billing is managed through the Stripe Dashboard and can be integrated using no-code subscription tools, Payment Links, Checkout, or a custom API integration

facts.label: Native app analytics SDKs
facts.value: No native iOS/Android event analytics SDK for Billing analytics is described; payment SDKs are separate from the billing reports

facts.label: Dashboard language list
facts.value: A complete list of Stripe Dashboard languages for Billing analytics was not found

facts.label: Deployment
facts.value: Vendor-hosted Stripe service; analytics are accessed in Stripe Dashboard

facts.label: Self-hosted edition
facts.value: No self-hosted or customer-operated Billing analytics edition is offered in the product, pricing, or documentation pages checked

facts.label: Website traffic reports
facts.value: Not applicable: Stripe Billing analytics reports subscription and billing data, not website visits, pageviews, referrals, or web campaigns

facts.label: Product behavior analytics and identity
facts.value: Not applicable as app-event analytics: Billing offers product/price revenue segmentation and subscriber/customer metrics, but its stated scope is billing data rather than feature-event funnels, paths, or behavioral identity stitching

facts.label: Session replay and heatmaps
facts.value: Not applicable: no visitor or in-app session recording product is part of Stripe Billing analytics

facts.label: Native mobile analytics SDK
facts.value: Not applicable: this is not a native app analytics collector

facts.label: Main Billing analytics measures
facts.value: Revenue, usage, subscribers, trials, churn, collections, and benchmarks; subscription analytics also supports MRR, churn rate, customer profiles, and subscriber counts

facts.label: Benchmark measures
facts.value: Built-in benchmarks include MRR growth rate, lifetime value, net MRR churn rate, and subscription payment failure rate

facts.label: MRR and ARR definitions
facts.value: MRR is the monthly-normalized recurring amount of active and past-due subscriptions; ARR is MRR × 12. Stripe notes MRR is a forward-looking performance metric, not GAAP revenue.

facts.label: MRR exclusions and churn rules
facts.value: Trials and usage-based metered charges are excluded from MRR; taxes and application fees do not count as revenue; subscriptions in unpaid status stop counting.

facts.label: Coupon treatment
facts.value: Businesses can configure whether recurring and one-time coupons reduce MRR; permanent recurring discounts are always subtracted

facts.label: Revenue recovery measures
facts.value: Failed payments, first-attempt failure rate, recovered payments, recovery rate, in-recovery payments, recovery method, top five decline codes, and customers currently in recovery

facts.label: Payment processor coverage
facts.value: Stripe Billing supports integration with multiple payment processors; the changelog says this became generally available in October 2025, while failed-payment/dunning support with third-party processors was marked preview

facts.label: Currency and FX treatment
facts.value: Exact currency normalization, exchange-rate timing, and multi-currency aggregation rules for Billing Analytics were not established in the metric pages checked

facts.label: Data setup
facts.value: Create subscription and billing records with the Dashboard, Payment Links, Checkout, or Billing API; Billing Analytics reports those records

facts.label: Usage metrics setup
facts.value: Basic usage-based records can be sent through Stripe Meters API; complex usage-based billing uses separate Metronome

facts.label: No analytics collector
facts.value: No separate browser script or native event SDK is required for the Billing analytics dashboard

facts.label: Data freshness
facts.value: Stripe Support says Billing Analytics data is available within one hour in most cases

facts.label: Best-case latency claim
facts.value: Stripe’s engineering blog described new subscription activity appearing with latency as low as 15 minutes when the streaming analytics system launched in September 2025

facts.label: MRR vs collected revenue
facts.value: MRR is normalized recurring subscription value, not cash receipts; tax, application fees, trial subscriptions, and metered usage are treated differently or excluded

facts.label: Sandbox data
facts.value: Subscriptions appear in the sandbox where they were created; deleting sandbox data means it will not register in Billing Analytics

facts.label: Website bot treatment
facts.value: Not applicable: these billing reports do not count website visits or filter website visitor bots

facts.label: Transaction sampling
facts.value: No general sampling rule for Billing Analytics transaction/subscription records was found in the reviewed product and support pages

facts.label: Browser script or SDK weight
facts.value: Not applicable: there is no Billing Analytics browser tracker or analytics SDK to measure

facts.label: Self-host maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: Stripe operates Billing analytics as a hosted service and publishes no customer-run deployment

facts.label: Browser cookies and visitor IDs
facts.value: Not applicable to Billing analytics as a website visitor collector; the service processes billing customer identifiers and personal data as part of Billing

facts.label: Customer notices and lawful basis
facts.value: Stripe’s DPA makes the Billing user responsible for providing customer notices and obtaining rights, permissions, and consents needed for lawful processing; the Stripe Billing terms also require relevant subscription disclosures to customers

facts.label: Analytics consent claim
facts.value: No general “cookie-free” or legally exempt analytics claim is made for Stripe Billing analytics

facts.label: Processing geography
facts.value: Stripe’s DPA says user data is transferred to Stripe, LLC in the United States and Stripe and affiliates may transfer it globally to affiliates and subprocessors

facts.label: Data residency and contracting entity
facts.value: Exact storage/backup regions for Billing Analytics are not set out in the reviewed product pages; Stripe’s contracting entity varies by account country/service

facts.label: DPA and subprocessors
facts.value: Stripe publishes a DPA and an updated subprocessor/affiliate list

facts.label: Data categories
facts.value: Stripe’s DPA lists payment/bank account details, billing/shipping address, name, order description/date/time/amount/product, device ID, email, IP/location, order ID, card details, tax status/ID, unique customer ID, and identity information where applicable

facts.label: Customer data deletion and return
facts.value: After termination, the DPA gives the user a choice for Stripe to delete or return personal data and delete existing copies, except where retention is required or authorized by law or needed to perform obligations

facts.label: Stripe API data access
facts.value: Stripe states the API enables users to programmatically access stored data for transfer, excluding PCI-scoped data

facts.label: Personal-data retention
facts.value: Stripe’s Privacy Center says it generally keeps personal data obtained from business users for five or more years after the business relationship ends or the last transaction, whichever is later, in most jurisdictions; other categories use different criteria

facts.label: Transaction-record retention
facts.value: Stripe says payment-service regulations require it to retain some transactional records for prescribed periods

facts.label: Billing Analytics history window
facts.value: A fixed maximum historical range for Billing Analytics charts or roll-forward downloads was not found in the product and support pages checked

facts.label: Termination and retention exceptions
facts.value: Following termination, Stripe may retain records where required or authorized by law or to perform post-termination obligations

facts.label: Billing fees and cancellation
facts.value: Stripe’s General Terms say payment obligations are non-cancelable and fees paid are non-refundable unless agreed otherwise or required by law

facts.label: Built-in report downloads
facts.value: Billing analytics supports download of MRR and active-subscriber roll-forward reports

facts.label: General Stripe report exports
facts.value: Stripe Dashboard reports can be viewed or downloaded as CSV; standard reports cover payments and financial activity, while Billing Analytics has its own metric reports

facts.label: API and warehouse access
facts.value: Underlying Stripe data is accessible through Stripe APIs; custom SQL reporting and warehouse sync use separately priced Sigma/Data Pipeline; a public API for every Billing Analytics chart was not identified

facts.label: Billing migration
facts.value: Stripe’s changelog says existing subscriptions can be migrated to Stripe Billing with a no-code migration toolkit

facts.label: Import of prior analytics history
facts.value: Whether prior MRR charts or analytics history from another billing/analytics provider can be imported into Billing Analytics was not found

facts.label: Name and URL
facts.value: Stripe Billing analytics; https://stripe.com/billing

facts.label: Operator and contracting entity
facts.value: Product operator: Stripe. The specific contracting Stripe entity depends on account country and service; the US entity is Stripe, LLC.

facts.label: Current availability
facts.value: Stripe currently offers Billing on pay-as-you-go and annual-subscription plans and links a self-serve start route

facts.label: Acquisition, shutdown, and sunset notices
facts.value: No Stripe Billing acquisition, shutdown, or sunset notice found in the official newsroom, blog/changelog, current Billing pages, or terms searched

facts.label: Stripe acquisition news
facts.value: Stripe completed its acquisition of Metronome on 2026-01-14; Metronome is a separate product for complex usage billing and is not included in Stripe Billing. Stripe also announced an agreement to acquire Parafin on 2026-09-30; that deal is not described as a Billing change.

facts.label: Current product activity
facts.value: Stripe’s official changelog has recent 2026 entries; Billing updates include benchmarks, usage analytics, and query/export options

facts.label: Source license
facts.value: No source license for Stripe’s hosted Billing analytics service is published; public Stripe SDKs do not establish an open-source license for the service itself

facts.label: Public documentation and support
facts.value: Stripe publishes Billing docs, support articles, product pages, release notes, and contact/support routes

facts.label: Public demo
facts.value: No public no-login Billing Analytics dashboard demo was identified on the product and pricing pages checked

facts.label: Offline event handling
facts.value: Maximum offline event queue, retry duration and loss behavior not established in pages checked

facts.label: Multiple-provider selection

facts.label: Gross sales definition

facts.label: MRR and ARR
facts.value: Subscription recurring revenue shown as MRR and annualized recurring revenue shown as ARR

facts.value: Realized LTV per new or paid user is net proceeds cohorted by install date; new dashboard supports fixed observation windows

facts.value: Refund Rate is refunds against gross proceeds by first purchase cohort; subscriber churn counts paid subscriptions expired in the period

facts.label: Currency treatment
facts.value: Original purchase currency and exact dashboard conversion source/FX date not established

facts.value: Stripe checkout can contribute to checkout/conversion analytics; current changelog notes custom-store purchases may report zero Superwall revenue unless tracked through that provider

facts.value: No general normalized MRR/ARR, revenue churn or third-party billing reconciliation formula established in subscription/sales docs checked.
